hypothesis: Bounded canonical map/reduce loops containing one four-block producer diamond can split before whole-loop vectorization legality or VPlan construction. Preserve the scalar header/two arms/common latch, materialize independent contributions at the latch, and let ordinary LV choose each stage independently. This admits integer-add and ordered float/double-add reductions with merged contributions, including an explicitly safe scalar helper lacking a vector mapping. Single-block support remains. Header and latch updates are both supported because the explicit CFG proves that each executes once per original iteration; arm-local or skipped updates remain rejected. No profitability gate, pressure threshold, chain-depth heuristic or original-loop vectorizability prerequisite is added.
semantics: The CFG check requires exactly four distinct blocks: the conditional header, two distinct arm blocks each with the header as its sole predecessor and an unconditional edge to the latch, and a common latch which alone exits or returns to the header. Single-block loops retain the existing path. Canonical zero-start/unit-step induction, guarded entry, exact eq/ne exit orientation, finite SCEV trip capacity, dedicated exits and LCSSA remain required. All producer blocks are scanned for the existing effect/call/live-out restrictions. Each accumulator PHI must have only its original add as a user, and that add may feed only its own recurrence and final LCSSA exports. Thus predicates, contribution PHIs and all other producer operations cannot depend on either old or updated accumulator state. Header/latch adds are unconditional; the original arm predicates, loads, arithmetic, helper calls and merge PHIs stay in place, with no speculation or neutral contributions. Scratch stores use merged values at the latch, and one existing ordered consumer clones operand order, wrap/FP flags, initial values, induction increment and exit comparison. LCSSA exports and predecessor rewrites now use the actual latch, including exports of header updates. Existing sibling-loop membership inside an outer loop, topmost-loop SE invalidation, block-disposition invalidation, dominator recalculation and caller loop-access-cache clearing are preserved. Strictfp functions/constrained operations remain rejected, with no errno/libm-name or extra fast-math assumptions. Both settings of the separate fission FP-reordering option must retain ordered results on this path. Executable verification is requested through the extended fixed-vscale checker: compare original scalar IR with the actual transformed diamond and exact consumer, assert independently located stage/scratch remarks, preserve the arm operations in IR, and insert host-only vector and scalar-tail consumer-header probes after PHIs. Cover all-division inputs with null untaken FP loads, all-load inputs with zero untaken divisors, alternating/runs/random arm sequences, exact integer/ordered FP results and canaries, zero/one/vector-boundary/tail/maximum/out-of-range counts, repeated calls, input/output aliasing, and repeated nested scratch reuse with real future-row input/output aliasing. Default EVL retains active-count/VP-load/ordered-reduction/progress assertions and RVV machine-verification RUNs, without host EVL execution.
costs: Full-trip static entry scratch remains bounded by the proven maximum and the existing checked byte ceiling (65536 bytes by default); no dynamic or unbounded allocation is added. Slots share identical contribution SSA values even when they are latch PHIs. The scalar_diamond fixture uses one 65*i32, one 65*double and one 65*float slot: 1044 accounted bytes including 4 alignment bytes, with 32*N logical scratch store-plus-load bytes per invocation. The two i64 contributions in diamond_arithmetic use 1040 bytes and 32*N logical traffic. scalar_diamond_nested uses 65*i32 plus 65*double: 784 accounted bytes including 4 alignment bytes, reused for every row, with 24*Rows*N logical traffic. Capacity does not multiply by Rows; entry allocations still contribute to the function frame when its guards bypass execution. The ceiling remains per candidate, not a new total-function-frame cap. Original integer loads execute once per participating iteration; FP loads and scalar helpers execute only on their original chosen arms. There are no original-input rereads, duplicated producer operations, recomputed contributions or new alias/SCEV guards. Loop control repeats for the consumer, and normal LV introduces independent stage vector/tail guards. The implementation adds a fixed four-block topology check, changes header-only scanning to a linear block/instruction/use scan, and reuses existing scratch/consumer emission, LI maintenance, SE invalidation and full-function dominator recalculation. No general predication machinery or new profitability model is introduced. Host-only probe calls perturb test code and are absent from RVV codegen artifacts; no performance inference is made.
limitations: No compiler, build, test runner, host executable or try.sh was invoked by this worker; all new results await independent harness validation. Static source/diff and whitespace review do not establish passing tests or corpus coverage. The new CFG support is exactly one block per arm, with header/latch updates; larger or chained CFGs, conditional participation, arm-local updates, internal cycles, early exits, noncanonical induction/exits, unsupported recurrences and non-final-reduction live-outs remain unsupported. Existing writes, volatile/atomic loads, unsafe/read-only-memory/indirect calls, strictfp/constrained FP and unsupported types remain rejected. There is no general masked-reduction or new FP-reassociation contract. Host execution is fixed-vscale scalar-tail specialization, not RVV target execution; the default EVL/VP path has IR and RVV codegen checks only. The specializer still rejects VP/EVL rather than approximating their semantics. VF=4 forces deterministic validation only and is not an implementation legality requirement. Actual automatically chosen producer VFs, unchanged-corpus effects and speedups are not claimed. Whole-trip scratch rather than bounded tiling remains the storage strategy.

test_expectations: New positive checks cover integer-only arithmetic with both header and latch updates, reversed exit orientation and preserved nuw/nsw/operand order; merged integer contributions shared by two sums; ordered float/double sums; a scalar helper without a vector mapping; and nesting with LCSSA outer carried values and alias stores. Scratch acceptance at 1044 bytes and rejection at 1043 bytes are explicit. Repeated vectorizer invocation and analysis verification guard stage markers and invalidation. A scalar-inspection RUN uses width one with an unspecified interleave hint and scalar interleave cap one: explicitly forcing width/interleave both to one would mark loops already vectorized and bypass early fission. Rejection cases retain correctness checks for conditional updates, old/updated accumulator control or PHI feedback, extra exits/cycles/cross-edges, stores, volatile/atomic loads, unsafe/readonly/errno-sensitive calls, constrained FP and merged/induction live-outs. The checker parser regression also requires probes after the exact vector/scalar-tail PHIs and rejects an arm division moved into the header. Existing lit expectations/correctness checks are retained; nested executable dispatch now carries its explicit reference function so both old and diamond fixtures are compared against their own original IR.
